Q: Adding a Line to Multiple Files in a Directory with an Extension A:

This seems to be working fine.

  1. It changes multiple files with the extension *.prm in the directory /mnt/hgfs/s3/bkp at the same time.

  2. If the line exists, it doesnt add it. I didnt even have to enable that check ahead of time. Fantastic!

---
    - name: Oracle GoldenGate add table to replicat, Process ID 2872.56
      hosts: localhost
      gather_facts: false
      vars_files:
        - vars/main.yml

      tasks:

      - name: Pass all GoldenGate parameter files to a variable array
        ansible.builtin.find:
          paths: "/mnt/hgfs/s3/bkp/"
          patterns: "*.prm"
          recurse: no
          file_type: file
        register: autofs_files
        delegate_to: localhost
        become: false

      - name: Debug GoldenGate parameter files
        debug:
          var: "{{ [item.path] }} "
        with_items: "{{ autofs_files.files }}"

      - name: Add an additional replication table mapping
        lineinfile:
          dest: "{{ item.path }}"
          line: MAP SOURCE.SOURCE_EXCLUDE1, TARGET TARGET.SOURCE_EXCLUDE1;
        with_items: "{{ autofs_files.files }}"
        register: etc_autofs
#        when: test_grep.stdout == "0"

Q: Handling of installId given by age_range_signals package in devices with multiple Gmail accounts logged in? A:

Your installID questions relate to Android docs:

  • It is "An ID assigned to supervised user", see usage for "age signals request": https://developer.android.com/google/play/age-signals/use-age-signals-api#request-age-signals

  • "Before revocation Google Play will include an installID in the Play Age Signals API (beta) response per user per device", see all cases and procedure: https://developer.android.com/google/play/age-signals/revoked-app-approval

Q: JavaScript - send ajax request without string concatenation A:

The data format is well documented and the standard JavaScript encodeURIComponent function will encode data for it.

jxobj.send('code=' + encodeURIComponent(code));

Is there any way to send ajax request without a string concatenation?

Not really. The send method takes a string, so you have to build a string using some mechanism or another. You could achieve it with (for instance) arrays and joins, but it still comes down to the same basic principles.

Q: PHP shorthand for isset && truthy A:

This is, of course, a short solution, but consider that short isn't the same as clear. When someone reads this code they might read it as: "check if $_POST['verylongname'] is not empty". It might not occur to them that you also want to make sure it is TRUE. How about:

($_POST['verylongname'] ?? FALSE) === TRUE

When it doesn't exist ?? will return FALSE, when it does exist it will return its value, from the parentheses. This is then compared against TRUE. This way you make it clear that the value must be TRUE.

In practice there's often no speed advantage in using shorter code. Your code uses two "operations"; a "not" operator and a function call. My code uses two as well; a null coalescing operator and a comparison.

I always choose readability above shortness when it comes to coding. Making your intentions clear in your code is important. That's why we write code in a higher programming language.
